subject: Add support for NSO Mega Drive Controller (#50)
author: Shig

impact.effect_if_absent: NSO Mega Drive/Genesis controller still works via vanilla 6.18's gencon support (joycon_type_is_gencon), but over BLUETOOTH reports the wrong product ID -- 0x2017/SNESCON instead of 0x201e/GENCON -- to the input layer, so Main_MiSTer's GUID-keyed gamecontrollerdb lookup matches the NSO SNES row and the pad comes out mismapped. Wired connections are unaffected (the PID is correct there), which is why this is easy to miss on the bench. RESOLVED 2026-07-24: carried as 0038.
affected_hardware: Nintendo Switch Online Mega Drive/Genesis Controller

userspace_coupling.interface: hdev->product (input device id.product field, propagated to input_dev->id.product at vanilla hid-nintendo.c:2134); consumed by Main_MiSTer's GUID-keyed SDL gamecontrollerdb lookup
userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref: Main_MiSTer/gamecontroller_db.cpp:544 gcdb_map_for_controller(bustype, vid, pid, version, ...) builds a GUID string directly from the raw (bustype,vid,pid,version) tuple (line 554: sprintf(guid_str, "%04x0000%04x0000%04x0000%04x0000", ...)) and looks it up in /media/fat/linux/gamecontrollerdb/gamecontrollerdb.txt (an external SDL-format community DB, not shipped in this repo); called from Main_MiSTer/input.cpp:3009 with input[sub_dev].pid, which is set at input.cpp:5197 from the kernel-reported id.product. A misreported PID therefore looks up a different GUID row than the physical device.

superseded_by: 94f18bb19945 (vanilla, 2023-12-04, 'HID: nintendo: add support for nso controllers')

notes:
DISPOSITION CORRECTED 2026-07-24 (fork-sync increment, docs/kernel-recon/fork-sync-2026-07.md §8.1): dropped-upstream -> carried.

WHAT WAS WRONG. The original pass graded this commit 'dropped-upstream' on the strength of mainline having NSO Genesis support (JOYCON_CTLR_TYPE_GEN, USB_DEVICE_ID_NINTENDO_GENCON, joycon_type_is_gencon) and set equivalence='partial' -- correctly noting in effect_if_absent and userspace_coupling that the Bluetooth PID normalisation was NOT covered. That is the grouped-conflation error this reconciliation exists to catch, in its subtler form: not a wholly-wrong citation, but a real upstream feature absorbing a MiSTer-specific behavioural hunk that has no mainline equivalent, with the un-covered remainder recorded as prose and then never actioned. 'partial' upstream coverage of a commit whose remainder is a live userspace-visible behaviour is a CARRY, not a drop.

THE UNCOVERED PIECE, verified against the live trees at v6.18.39: `grep -c 'hdev->product = ' drivers/hid/hid-nintendo.c` returns 0 -- vanilla never rewrites the PID anywhere in the file. Stock DOES, at MiSTer-v5.15 hid-nintendo.c:1761-1765: '/* MD controller has wrong PID via BT, so just force it */ if (hdev->product == USB_DEVICE_ID_NINTENDO_SNESCON && ctlr->ctlr_type == JOYCON_CTLR_TYPE_MD) { hdev->product = USB_DEVICE_ID_NINTENDO_MDCON; }'. So this was a genuine STOCK-PARITY GAP -- a silent regression our image shipped -- not merely an enhancement.

NAMING, which is what made the gap easy to miss: stock calls the device MDCON (hid-ids.h:936, 0x201E) where mainline calls it GENCON (hid-ids.h:1067, 0x201e) -- the same PID, renamed when NSO support landed upstream. Stock's JOYCON_CTLR_TYPE_MD (hid-nintendo.c:311) and mainline's JOYCON_CTLR_TYPE_GEN (hid-nintendo.c:322) are likewise the same wire value, 0x0D. A search for stock's identifiers in the 6.18 tree finds nothing and reads as 'absent upstream'; a search for the device finds it and reads as 'covered'. Both are half-right.

CARRIED AS 0038-hid-nintendo-nso-genesis-bt-pid.patch, re-implemented against 6.18's joycon_input_create() using the mainline GENCON/TYPE_GEN names and placed immediately before devm_input_allocate_device() so id.product is already correct when the input_dev is populated. Verified: all 32 patches in the series apply cleanly to a pristine v6.18.39 worktree via `git am`, and drivers/hid/hid-nintendo.o cross-compiles clean with the Buildroot arm-buildroot-linux-gnueabihf toolchain against the image's own .config. Bench verification with a real NSO Genesis pad over Bluetooth is still outstanding.

HOW IT SURFACED: not by re-reading this record, but by tree-diffing our export against Sorgelig's independent 6.18 forward-port -- upstream's port carries the normalisation, ours did not. The 2026-07-24 adversarial verification pass flagged the difference; the stock-parity significance was established afterwards by checking MiSTer-v5.15 directly. orchestrator-verified (Opus 5, 2026-07-24): corrected (disposition dropped-upstream -> carried; gap closed by 0038).
sonnet-verified: corrected -- SHA/ancestry, line citations (hid-nintendo.c:322, hid-ids.h:1067), the doc-disagreement/grouped-row flag, and the core partial-equivalence disposition all confirmed accurate; the open question the prior pass left unresolved ('does the product-ID workaround matter for a real consumer') is now answered definitively YES with a path:line citation (gamecontroller_db.cpp:544/554, input.cpp:3009/5197) and a concrete carry recommendation added to notes and userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref.
